claim: Public CSA implementations materialize a [B, S, HI, T] FP32 indexer score tensor before the top-k reduction; with V4-Flash dimensions (HI=64, compression m=4) that intermediate is 256 GB at S=65,536 and 1 TB at S=131,072 on a single batch.
stance_target: The assumption that the attention kernel is the binding constraint for CSA at long context
scope_conditions: V4-Flash reference indexer code path (references/DeepSeek-V4-Flash/inference/model.py lines 415-423); B=1, HI=64, T=S/4, FP32
quoted_support: The first line produces a [B, S, HI, T] FP32 tensor; the second reduces over HI. With V4-Flash dimensions (B=1, HI=64, T=S/4), this intermediate is 256 GB at S=65,536 and 4 TB at S=262,144.

claim: At S=32,768 with V4-Flash dimensions the materialize indexer produces a 64 GB intermediate before the head-sum and peaks at 129 GB HBM on a 140 GB H200 — i.e. even at 32k the naive CSA indexer needs roughly twice the HBM of a single 64 GB CMP 170HX card.
stance_target: The repo's implicit assumption that a 32k CSA2 experiment fits inside one 64 GB card's activation budget
scope_conditions: Single H200 SXM 140 GB HBM3e, BF16 inputs, synthetic-but-realistic V4-shaped inputs, peak measured with torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated
quoted_support: At S=32K where both fit, the chunked path is also faster (10.3x). This is because the materialize path produces a 64 GB intermediate before the head-sum, then a separate 1 GB intermediate after.

claim: The indexer step, not the attention kernel, gates the maximum sequence length a CSA pipeline can run: the pipeline runs out of memory in the indexer before attention executes.
stance_target: Optimizing the sparse attention kernel first when planning a CSA experiment
scope_conditions: V4-Flash dimensions on a single H200
quoted_support: Assuming attention is the bottleneck at long context is incorrect for CSA: the pipeline runs out of memory in the indexer step before attention runs.

claim: Every public CSA pipeline the authors know of OOMs on a single H200 (140 GB) for S >= 64K with V4-Flash dimensions, before the top-k is selected and before any attention runs.
stance_target: The claim that CSA at long context is memory-gated rather than compute-gated
scope_conditions: Survey of public CSA implementations; single H200 140 GB HBM
quoted_support: Every public CSA pipeline we are aware of OOMs on a single H200 (140 GB HBM) for S >=64K with V4-Flash dimensions, before the top-k has been selected, before any attention has run.

claim: A chunked partition-merge top-k driver is exact because the lightning-indexer score is per-key separable — once the query is fixed the score is a pure function of the key index, with no softmax or normalization coupling across keys — so per-tile top-k can be merged without approximation.
stance_target: Feasibility of a streaming/chunked top-k implementation on memory-constrained hardware
scope_conditions: Lightning indexer score definition; partition-merge invariance theorem
quoted_support: The lightning-indexer score is per-key separable: once the query is fixed, the score is a pure function of the key index, with no inter-key coupling (no softmax, no normalization that mixes scores). This separability makes the top-k commute with iteration order.

claim: The chunked indexer runs the same V4-Flash indexer to S=1,048,576 at 6.21 GB peak HBM, a 32x regime extension over the materialize path's OOM at S=65,536.
stance_target: That a 32k CSA experiment on a 64 GB card is feasible with a chunked top-k implementation
scope_conditions: Single H200 SXM 140 GB, BF16, CUDA 13, Triton 3.7, PyTorch 2.13 nightly; cS=2048, cT=8192
quoted_support: the materialize indexer OOMs at S=65,536, our chunked indexer runs at S=1,048,576 with 6.21 GB peak HBM, a 32x regime extension.

claim: FP32 score accumulation is required for exact top-k parity: FP16 accumulation drops perfect-recall rows from 99.99% to 91.82%.
stance_target: Precision requirements for a chunked CSA indexer implementation
scope_conditions: Ablation study at V4-Flash dimensions, S=262,144
quoted_support: FP32 score accumulation is necessary (FP16 drops perfect-recall rows from 99.99% to 91.82%).

claim: Set-overlap recall against the materialize ground truth is bit-exact at small S where both fit, and across three 5-point design-space sweeps mean recall rounds to 1.0000 with minimum recall at least 0.9980 in every cell.
stance_target: That chunked top-k does not change model behaviour versus the reference implementation
scope_conditions: Sweeps over chunk size, key-tile size, top-k; synthetic-but-realistic V4-shaped inputs
quoted_support: Set-overlap recall against the materialize ground truth is bit-exact at small S where both fit; across three 5-point design-space sweeps (chunk size, key-tile size, top-k), mean recall rounds to 1.0000 with min recall at least 0.9980 in every cell.

claim: Chunk size has a clear knee around cS=2048; a single chunk over T is optimal when memory allows; and a per-chunk causal mask keeps mask memory at O(cS*cT) instead of O(S*T), which is what lets the chunked path scale past S=131,072.
stance_target: Tuning guidance for implementing a chunked CSA indexer
scope_conditions: Design-space sweeps and ablations at V4-Flash dimensions
quoted_support: A design-space and ablation study (3 sweeps, 3 ablations) showing that chunk size has a clear knee around cS=2048, single-chunk over T is optimal when memory allows, and FP32 score accumulation is necessary.
